new_findings.text: Reproducibility is identified as a critical new frontier for effective AI governance, with weak reproducibility protocols undermining policymakers' ability to enact meaningful policy.
new_findings.evidence: Current publication speeds in AI combined with lack of strong scientific standards via weak reproducibility protocols erodes policymakers' power to enact meaningful governance protocols.

new_findings.text: Global AI governance is characterized by a "Global AI Divide" with systemic inequities in education, digital infrastructure, and access to decision-making processes that perpetuate dependency and exclusion for Global Majority countries.
new_findings.evidence: Analysis highlights disparities in AI development, innovation, and regulation, focusing on systemic inequities in education, digital infrastructure, and access to decision-making processes.

new_findings.text: Stricter reproducibility guidelines in AI research are proposed as a concrete mechanism to assist governance endeavors and improve consensus on the AI risk landscape.
new_findings.evidence: Paper outlines how AI research could adopt stricter reproducibility guidelines to assist governance endeavours and improve consensus on the AI risk landscape.

new_findings.text: The current AI information environment for policymakers suffers from low Signal-To-Noise Ratio, favoring regulatory capture and creating deep uncertainty about risk prioritization.
new_findings.evidence: Information environment offered to policymakers characterised by unnecessarily low Signal-To-Noise Ratio, favouring regulatory capture and creating deep uncertainty and divides on which risks should be prioritised.

new_findings.text: Global Majority countries face a dependency and exclusion cycle in international AI governance due to disparities in capacity and representation.
new_findings.evidence: Systemic inequities in education, digital infrastructure, and access to decision-making processes perpetuate a dependency and exclusion cycle for Global Majority countries.

new_findings.text: AI adoption in workplaces is rapidly changing job responsibilities, with explicit AI mentions in job postings increasing 66% (2023-2025), though much growth occurs outside actual work activity descriptions.
new_findings.evidence: Explicit mentions of AI increased by 66% in job advertisements from 33 firms between 2023 and 2025, though much growth occurs outside descriptions of actual work activities.

new_findings.text: OSCAL (NIST standard for FedRAMP) proposed as machine-readable interchange format for AI governance compliance evidence, with 16 property extensions covering lifecycle phases, enforcement semantics, risk traceability, and risk-acceptance justification
new_findings.evidence: Paper proposes OSCAL as candidate interchange format for AI governance, complementing JTC21 standards stack; defines 16 property extensions and three-layer Compliance-as-Code architecture (policy, evidence, enforcement) that generates assurance evidence as machine-readable artifacts

new_findings.text: AI incident governance lacks consistent definitions, taxonomies, monitoring practices, and reporting mechanisms across regulatory and independent frameworks
new_findings.evidence: Survey of existing AI incident governance frameworks finds inconsistencies in incident data collection, categorization, and analysis depth/representativeness/accuracy

new_findings.text: Reproducibility identified as critical frontier for AI governance to reduce signal-to-noise ratio in policy information environment and mitigate regulatory capture
new_findings.evidence: Paper argues reproducibility is new frontier in AI governance, linking low reproducibility to deep uncertainty in risk prioritization

new_findings.text: Generative AI Toolkit proposed as framework automating essential workflows for LLM-based applications across full lifecycle (development, maintenance, operations)
new_findings.evidence: Paper introduces Generative AI Toolkit to address manual, slow, trial-and-error DevOps workflows for LLM applications, aiming to increase quality and scalability
